subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Perhaps that word was
wrongly used. We might say that they are, but not deliberately so. Some of them are.
I would not think the aerodrome at St. Johns, Quebec, would be strategically located from that point of view, nor would the Chatham location be particularly well strategically located.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: That is the air training school?

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: The air observer school. The question is, are they strategically located so as to be of commercial value to these companies after the war? I do not know that Chatham and St. Johns are particularly well located for that purpose. I suppose that, as far as the west is concerned, almost anywhere on the prairies would be a strategic location for an aerodrome.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: What the minister is saying is that they were not located in the first instance having that factor in view?

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: No.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
While I
am on my feet I want to refer to the Pennfield Ridge station. The minister yesterday indicated that the field could not be used for the purposes for which it was designed because of lack of sunshine.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Stars, I think it was. Astro-navigation.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I understand the position was that it was not advantageous to use the location because of the height of the clouds.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: That is right.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: That is an entirely different matter. I should like to have that made absolutely clear.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I stand corrected.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Because
the clouds there are two or three miles high, too high for the operational training which was going on there. I would not want to have it understood that it was lack of sunshine or that the stars were too far away. I understand that the school has been moved to Rivers, Manitoba, where another condition obtains. What use is being made of the very expensive plant?

War Appropriation-Air Services

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
It is going to be put to
full use.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: It cost a tremendous amount of money. The work could have been done a good deal cheaper if it had been done by tender. However, I am not criticizing.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: That is true. I am willing to agree with that.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: But speed is the important factor, not the dollar cost. What is it being used for now?

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
It is being put to very
good use.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: The minister does not care to say.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: It is being used for operational training.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Since the questions to the Minister of National Defence for Air are now pretty well completed, I should like to say on behalf of the Thunder Bay district, which has two leading cities, Fort William and Port Arthur, that we are extremely proud of the Minister of Munitions and Supply. When anybody honours him we appreciate it, and when people criticize him without sense we watch them and pity them. We at the head of the lakes, and I am sure every hon. member in this chamber, will congratulate the minister upon having received from Clarkson college the degree of Doctor of Engineering.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: He is being educated by degrees.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
We wish him good success
under the direction of the Great Architect of the Universe, that he may' be long spared to carry on and keep things running smoothly, because he has always command of a sufficient quantity of oil for troubled waters.

speechtext: What are the various ranks in the fighting air force called? For instance, what is the highest rank to which a man can attain in the air force?

I think it is Air Chief
Marshal of England, and I believe it can be held only by His Majesty the King. But I am not sure of that.

speechtext:
Is it equivalent
to general, or admiral, or what?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
I believe that Air Chief
Marshal of England is the very highest rank. I am not sure if that is the correct title.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Then is
there not an air vice-marshal?

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Then there are air chief
marshals. Really, I cannot tell the hon. member; I do not know. I shall never attain to those titles, in any event.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
What are the
rates of pay of the various ranks?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Speaking
of Canada.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Per day'. It runs about the same as in the army'. I believe there is some arrangement whereby the pay is much the same as that of equivalent ranks in the army.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Would
an air vice-marshal get about the same as a major-general? We have one or two air vice-marshals.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Yes; he is paid about the
same as a major-general. The only air marshal we have is the chief of the air staff; he is on a consolidated rate of pay, just as are the head of the navy and the head of the army.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
What do the
schoolteachers get?

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I do not know.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I mean, the persons who are appointed to teach mathematics and who are made flight lieutenants and so on.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: It depends on the rank.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Are they classified as officers?

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
It all depends whether the
man has a commission. I do not know.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
I cannot see the
reason for such a proceeding. I know that men require this type of training, but I cannot see why a schoolteacher who goes into the air force for three or four months is promptly

War Appropriation-Air Services
made a flight lieutenant, while the men whom he teaches are flying over Berlin soon afterwards at a sergeant's rate of pay.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY

army who remains in Canada as an instructor get a commission as a lieutenant or a captain if he remains here for instructional purposes? I suppose, for the same reason. There is no difference in principle.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence

commodore.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Is that the only method of securing information? speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY

speechtext: Is the cost of building and maintaining airports in Canada paid through the department of the minister?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Is the air force taking steps to prepare for the training of paratroops?

speechtext: I know that in the old country that is the army's job. We are not doing it.

speechtext: But is the home war establishment of the air force in a position to train paratroops?

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
I hardly think so. We have not been asked.

War Appropriation-Air Services

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Have we any planes that could carry them?

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I do not know.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Are the members of the air force or of the army stationed at either coast regarded as being on an actual war footing?

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I do not know what my hon. friend means.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: What I am leading up to is this. When a soldier is overseas-I do not mean in Newfoundland-he does not pay the national defence tax, and I cannot see why men in British Columbia should pay it.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I am not sure about the national defence tax, but there was a lot of difficulty about the income tax. It was considered that when a man was in an actual theatre of war he would not pay income tax. The Atlantic coast was considered to be an actual theatre of war and, I believe, the Pacific coast also. But that was not satisfactory because there were so many changes, and they got it down to the basis of so many flying hours. I cannot explain it to my hon. friend. It has been explained to me ten times and I do not understand it. It is based on the number of flying hours, and the question of income tax and the national defence tax, perhaps, is on a similar basis.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I have yet to see anything that the minister could not explain.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: If I cannot understand it myself I cannot explain it.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: The minister might find an explanation that would not be satisfactory to me, but he would find an explanation. I had a letter yesterday in that connection from some of his own people. We are doing as good work in patrolling the Pacific and the Atlantic for submarines and what have you, as anyone else is doing, and I cannot see why these men should not have exemption from national defence tax. If they patrol hundreds of miles out on the Atlantic or the Pacific they are taking the same chance as other men.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I think they are getting it, but I do not know in what form.

speechtext:
The minister told us yesterday that the air force was experimenting with the use of gliders. In view of the hazards of shipping our fighter planes overseas, has it considered the possibility of using gliders to carry extra fuel in order that our fighter planes may travel under

their own power? I understand that has been worked out by the axis powers and is used extensively.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I do not know, but if I did I am afraid I could not tell my hon. friend anyway.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: A few weeks ago we had complaints on the Pacific coast that men of the ground crews, mechanics and other skilled men, were being used at some of the coast bases for making roads. There might have been some reason for that, but on its face it does not seem reasonable. Perhaps labour companies or some similar formations should be set up to do that type of work. Why are trained men, skilled mechanics, used in that way? It is hard on the morale of the men in the force, and it is difficult to explain to the general public.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I cannot tell my hon. friend, but I am sure that if they were used to any great extent I would have heard about it.

PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: If they are not busy at something else, would it hurt them to build roads?

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Not a bit.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: But when mechanics are so badly needed, if not in the air force at any rate in the army, they should not be put on that work.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: They may not have a steady job working at mechanics the whole day. If they have six aircraft that do nut go up for six days because of six days of fog, they might just as well do a little bit of work on the roads while the fog is on. There is fog in British Columbia too.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Would the minister answer a question I raised regarding the cost of living bonus to the dependents of airmen?

speechtext:
That is a big question. I would have to take it up with my colleague, the Minister of National Defence, and particularly with my colleague the Minister of Finance. He is' the man to answer that question.

Privilege-Mr. Church

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
Since speaking about the situation of those Canadians who are enlisted with the Royal Air Force, I find that some 500 or 600 approximately left Canada at the outbreak of war and enlisted in the R.A.F. in the old country. I suppose there are many men there who feel this discrepancy of lower rates of pay plus the British income tax. The number must be considerable, and these men are not able to speak for themselves. I hope the minister will give serious consideration to the matter. It is possible that some men do not wish to remuster in the R.CA.F. but to those who do-and some do prefer to remuster- I hope every consideration will be given because these men have shown, if you will, an excess of loyalty. They were the first to volunteer when the war broke out, and everything should be done to put them on an equal basis with those who have gone over since.
I would bring to the attention of the minister a point raised by the hon. member for Broadview (Mr. Church) as to whether or not consideration is being given to forming a Royal Canadian Air Force regiment such as they have in the old country for the protection of aerodromes. I am not stating that there is a positive need for this at the present time, but I should like to hear from the minister what consideration has been given to the matter of protecting our aerodromes against possible raids, say from aircraft carriers, and whether any consideration has been given to the formation of a regiment.

speakerposition: Associate Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Air; Minister of National Defence for Air and Associate Minister of National Defence
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: At the present time we look after internal security wdthin the perimeter of the aerodrome, sabotage and that kind of thing, while the army defends us against anything else.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO PUS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
On the
question of remustering of Canadians, I have in mind a very gallant young Canadian who went over on his own before the war. I think I told the story in this house when I came back from England. He is now a squadron leader. He has won the distinguished flying cross. In a conversation I had with him he wanted to know what future there was for him and men like him in Canada after the war. Certainly there will not be much opportunity for him in England, unless he wins great distinction there and gets further promotion, because there are so many in competition with him. If such a young man, coming back to this country after a distinguished career, could be allowed to remuster into a Canadian force, he would have a chance for the future, which he thinks lies in that direction. I merely mention him as an 'illustration
of many boys who, like him, went over on their own before the war. Let them get into the Royal Canadian Air Force. Then, when the war is ended, if they are fortunate enough to be alive they will come back to Canada as members of the Royal Canadian Air Force. It seems to me that a unique opportunity to consider and discuss this matter is afforded in connection with this coming conference.
Progress reported.
